utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic and Vladimir Santic also know as "Vlado".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. Counsel Puliselic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Before we begin the examination of the witness, I would like to introduce Mrs. Nika Pinter, my co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. Welcome to your court. Mr. Moskowitz?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: We too. Prosecution also welcomes Defence counsel to the Court. With regard to two orders that were introduced by the Prosecution and accepted into evidence, that would be Exhibit 251 and Exhibit 252, I believe the Court has requested us, the Prosecution, to determine whether there are any originals available, and I would like to report back to the Court on what our investigation has revealed to date, which is that these two exhibits were, in fact, tendered as Defence exhibits in the Blaskic case. They were tendered as copies, not as originals, and, therefore, there are, as far as we know, no originals yet available either to the Defence in Blaskic or if they're available to the Defence in Blaskic they have not as yet produced them. We do not have originals, and it's our information that those exhibits were tendered but not yet admitted into evidence because of a witness who could not authenticate them, but that, in fact, there is a witness testifying at this time dealing with these exhibits and they may be admitted at that time. But as to whether there are originals, at this time, there are no originals that we know of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness EE.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, I would like to start with the events of April 16, 1993. To assist you in your testimony, I would ask that the usher provide you with the diagram of your house, which is Exhibit 275. Now, from time to time I will ask you to refer to that diagram, but you need not be referring to it all the time. Now, I want you to think back to April 16, 1993, and could you tell us where you were that morning before the attack started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were on the first floor of our house, in the bedroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: By "we," who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I mean my husband, and my children and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us what the first thing you remember of that morning, the first thing you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first thing was a strong detonation and shooting. A strong detonation first, followed by shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What do you recall doing, or hearing, or seeing next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the same instance we all jumped up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What did you do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I grabbed my children by their shoulders, my husband was in front of me, and I went out into the hallway. We tried to go into the bathroom up above, on the floor above. I opened the door and the bullets were already firing through the bathroom window and going into the wall. I automatically shut the door, got my children away and we returned to the hallway, on the landing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, when you say you opened the door, which door are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: The bathroom door on the floor above.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, after you closed the door of the bathroom and pulled your children away, what do you remember next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't push my children, I kept holding on to them by the shoulders, and all four of us went down the stairs into the lower hallway, that is the floor below, and we stood in the hallway there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: While you stood in the hallway there, you and your family, did you hear or see anything at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: We stood in the hallway and we were mute, just looking at each other. Then there were terrible voices to be heard, terrible voices, and I can hear them even now. They called out my husband's name. They called him, "Open the door, this is the police." This was repeated several times, but we kept quiet because we were terribly afraid by this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: When you heard your husband's name being called, what were you thinking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I saw that nothing nice was happening. It was terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What did your husband do next, or what did you do, or what did you see or hear next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: As we didn't say anything and there were these voices shouting, suddenly there was a burst of gunfire. This part here is in glass, it is a glass partition. This is a wall, and up above the wall was glass panes. There was a large door and part of the door was in glass as well. The bursts of gunfire reverberated against the glass and the doors fell off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you're referring to the part of the diagram that has the number 2 on it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's right. From these steps they were firing at the door, and, of course, the bullets hit the glass panelling and so the glass shattered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Where were you and your family when you heard that firing from outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: We have a hallway here (indicating). From that hallway was the door leading to the garage, and to the living-room, and to the kitchen, and the door to the bathroom, and a door to a storage place which had ceramic tiling in it. At that particular point we were in this hallway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Was the door leading into the main part of the house, marked number 1, was that doorway at that time open or closed when you heard the firing from outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. When they started shooting at the glass and the door fell -- caved in, my husband unlocked this other door. As he unlocked it, he opened the door, he was standing here, my children and I were here, and I kept holding the children mechanically. I felt that my fist mechanism had become rigid, had locked. When my husband opened the door, I saw, in this part here, soldiers in full military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, perhaps, with the help of the usher, I will ask you to take one of those markers, perhaps the orange one would show up best, and do a couple of things for us. Could you put an X where your husband was standing when he opened the door that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you put the letter "A" where you were standing with your children when your husband opened the door and you saw soldiers? Just the letter "A" so we can place your position first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: The position was here (marks).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you put a circle in the area where you saw soldiers when your husband opened the door? Make it, I guess, big enough to include the general area where the soldiers were standing when you saw them, so we know how big an area they occupied. You can make a large circle or a small circle, whatever you think is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: You want me to place a circle; is that right? I didn't quite understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes. A circle to show, in the general area, where the soldiers were standing when you saw them when your husband opened the door, again, using the marker.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, when your husband opened the door and you saw those men standing there, about how long did you have to see them before your eyes shifted to something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was seconds, a the matter of seconds. Very quick. When my husband opened the door, I looked at them all like this, as I'm -- this way. When he open the door, I looked at them, I looked at all of them, and I was dumbfounded. Nobody said anything. My husband didn't say anything, they didn't say anything, the children didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: When you looked at these men, these soldiers, for those two seconds or so, did you form an impression as to who these soldiers were at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Who did you recognise standing there at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Vlado Santic, Zeljo Livancic, Drago Josipovic, Marinko Katava, Karlo Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At that time did you recognise anyone else in those two seconds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: At this moment I just cannot think. I know Katava was there, Cerkez was there, Zeljo, Santic, Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, when your husband opened the door you saw these soldiers standing there --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: -- what did you see happen next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Santic and Zeljo -- my husband was standing here. That's where they were (indicating). They had freed this area here. It was all a matter of seconds. They just turned round in a circle, the two of them. My husband went in front of them, and Zeljo, and Vlado Santic went behind him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: How were these two men, Zeljo Livancic and Vlado Santic, dressed that morning, as you recall now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I remember. It was a camouflage uniform with an HVO patch, and they had helmets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did any of the other soldiers standing on your veranda, or your porch, have helmets that morning, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, only those two. I saw those two, and they were wearing helmets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you say that these two men who were wearing helmets, Vlado Santic and Zeljo Livancic, took your husband. In which direction did you see them take your husband? If you could point for us, just to show us the direction in which they went.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can just show you as much as I saw. My glance went up to these -- I could see up to these steps here. I call it the veranda. We had sort of a plateau, a plate, and then an entrance door, and I was on this plateau and that's where I saw my husband for the last time. I never saw or heard of him again after that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you take the marker in front you, and with an arrow, show us the direction in which you saw your husband go with those two men when you saw your husband for the last time, just so that we know the direction.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Perhaps another marker would be better. Not a pencil, but a marker.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you put an arrow mark on it so we know which direction you're referring to, using, again, the blue marker. At the end of that line, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, what is the next thing you remember seeing or hearing after you saw your husband being led away in that direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I remember him saying, "Don't kill my wife and children."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That would be your husband who said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, my husband said that; "Don't kill my wife and children."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could I interrupt for one second? Do you remember what your husband was wearing that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course I do. Of course I remember. He had a vest and short pants on. Of course I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Was he dressed in civilian clothes or in a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Your husband.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: My husband was sleeping, and he slept in his under-vest, his underwear, his vest and short pants, and that's how he got up, in his underwear. It all happened in a matter of seconds. That's how he was taken out and that's how he was killed. You can carry out an identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did he have a weapon, your husband, when he was taken away or when he went to the door that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, no. We didn't have any weapons of any kind, any arms of any kind. My husband worked on the 15th of April, 1993, and he came back from work in the evening, towards evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, let's get back to what happened that morning. When your husband was led away, what is the next thing you remember seeing or hearing after that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: The moment he was taken away, and this was very fast, Drago Josipovic told me, "Go into that corner, that corner over there, and we're going to slaughter all of you," and that's the corner he meant, this corner here (indicating). "You three go into that corner, and we're going to cut your throats."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Where was Drago Josipovic standing when you heard him order you to go into the corner? Again, if you could use your pointer to show us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were standing here. There (indicating). When he was taken away, they drew closer to me. I was ordered to go into this corner with my children, and they said they would cut our throats.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you go into the corner as you were told to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Where were your children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I kept a firm hold on my children. I never let them go for one second. I kept this mechanical hold on them. The moment that we had got up out of bed and I got hold of them by the shoulder, I never let them go until I had reached the shed over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you take that marker in front of you now and place the letter "B" where you and your children went after you were told to go into the corner, so that we can have this for the record and refer to it later on. Could you put the letter "B" there so we know, when we read the record, that that is the second position you were at that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: While you were at that corner, position "B," which is on the veranda, what do you recall hearing or seeing next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was passing here and my back was turned. We came to this point and turned round. When I had turned round, at that very second, there was only one HVO soldier standing here, just one, and he looked at me like this. This was Stipo Alilovic, nicknamed Brko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: How long did you look at this Stipo Alilovic at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just for several seconds. It was a matter of seconds. It wasn't slow motion. Everything occurred in a matter of seconds. Everything they did, this whole operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What do you recall seeing or hearing next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps a second or two or three, it's very hard for me to tell the time, in one split second, again a group of soldiers appeared. Stipo Alilovic stood leaning against this wall at this first step. Zeljo Livancic stood next to him. After him was Drago Josipovic and Karlo Cerkez at that point. Then I spoke up and I said, "People, what is this? What is going on?" They were just staring at me. They didn't say a word. They stared and stared and stared. This Brko, Alilovic Stipo, held a bomb, a grenade, in this hand, next to him was Zeljo, and he says this -- he was staring, staring. They stood and stared, when I said, "People, what is this? What is going on? Why is this going on?" Stipo Alilovic came up and said, "What do I do with the grenade?" he says to Zeljo. Zeljo looked at us this way, looked at me, looked at my children. I'm sorry, I apologise for using this word. He says, "Out. Get lost."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Who did he say that to, "Get lost" or "Out"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: To me and to my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Who said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Zeljo Livancic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Who is Zeljo Livancic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: When Zeljo Livancic ordered you to get out, what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: As I was clutching my children, I started walking this way, to this veranda, as we call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you go down the stairs of the veranda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not all the stairs, you know. They stood there, and, as I was holding my children, I walked out this way and I went this way (indicating). One was supposed to jump a bit, but I wasn't really very careful at that point, so I took my children and we went a bit to the other side -- or, rather, it is direct, but, you know, they were standing there. So we went out this way (indicating), and they were getting into the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, when you passed by the soldiers as you were going down the veranda, did you look at them as you walked past them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't, I didn't. I was holding my children, and I just looked straight ahead of myself. When I was crouching here with my children, that is when we saw each other, and also when I said, "People, what is this? What is going on? Why is this going on?" as I was saying that, they remained silent. They looked at each other. Then Stipo Alilovic asked what I already told you about, what he'd do with the hand grenade. Zeljo looked at me and the children and he said, "Out. Get out."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, earlier you had said that, when your husband was taken away, Zeljo Livancic was one of the two men that took him. Had he then returned to the veranda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. He came back. As he was taken away and as they were ordering me to go here and there and I crouched there with my children, when I crouched there, only Stipo was there. In a moment, they reappeared, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, what about the second man who took your husband, Vlado Santic? At the time you were on the veranda in position "B" and as you left the veranda, had Vlado Santic returned or was he still not there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: He did not return then. He did not return then. Only they came back, and I went out here (indicating). This is where my mother stood who had already been evicted from her house. She had been wounded a bit. They had opened her house by shooting at her door and shooting her door down and she had burns on her face, and she was crouching there and she watched our fate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you help us again and take the marker and put a "C," the letter "C," where you went, you and your children went after you were ordered to leave the veranda, so that we know where you and your children were next? The letter "C."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That would be just near the room or the area marked number 8 on the schematic of your house and stables; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. This is where my children and I were and my mother. Actually, I came with my children to my mother as she had already been crouching there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Where had your mother been; do you know? When you saw her at that position "C," where had she been before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Her house was right here, near mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Right next door to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. My house was here and her house was right here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did your mother say anything to you when you met her at position "C"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we came to her, bullets were flying all over. We leaned hard against this wall here, and I felt a soldier walking up, marching up, and as he passed here, this part here (indicating), I raised my head and I saw Mr. Santic, and I said, "Santic! Santic! Vlado!" Vlado looked at me just like this, and he jumped away from me, three metres away from me. He jumped towards Zarko's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you put a "V" where you saw and spoke with Vlado Santic that morning so we know where that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, which Vlado Santic are we talking about? because there are several Vlado Santics in the area of Vitez. Which Vlado Santic are you referring to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what you are exactly interested in. Vlado is here, whose father-in-law lived below my house. That was a wonderful man, his father-in-law, a very honest man. A truly good man, you know, his father-in-law. He's the one. And the other one, as far as I know, his wife had a kiosk where they sold literature and cigarettes, and I was in charge of the private sector at the Vitez municipality, and when something was needed, Vlado Santic, who was there, near my house, he would come to take care of these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you know what position Vlado -- this Vlado Santic had prior to the attack in Ahmici in 1993, what his job was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was in the HVO police. I think he was commander of the HVO police. My office was facing the post office, the hotel, and I would often see him passing along the street towards the hotel because I also worked until the very last day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you describe what this Vlado Santic looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, he was sort of a bigish lad with a firm footstep, blond, a high forehead. Like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you see him in the courtroom today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you describe where he's sitting or what he's wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He's wearing a necktie, he's wearing a jacket, a darker jacket, he has headphones on his ears. Is that sufficient? A white shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us a little more about his facial appearance so that we know you're identifying --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Fair complexion, a fair complexion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What about hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: He doesn't really have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: May the record reflect that she has identified Vlado Santic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You have also talked about Drago Josipovic. Do you see him here in the courtroom today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you describe him please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Mr. Drago is sitting behind this pillar here. He has a moustache, white shirt and a tie, and also a jacket like Vlado.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: May the record reflect that she has identified Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Now that we're on the subject of Drago Josipovic, can I say something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Before the conflict, Mr. Drago Josipovic was going home from work with Fahrudin Ahmic. They were talking. As they came to our houses -- because our houses were first by the road and then their houses -- Drago Josipovic told Fahrudin, "Pity for these two houses down here." Fahrudin answered, "Drago, you say what you know." Fahrudin swore a bit too, you know, he said, "Drago, tell me, you know something." Fahrudin came to us and he told us about that immediately. That is what I wish to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: So you heard this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the statement of this witness because this is hearsay. It comes from another person because she is telling us what another person told her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, I think on at least three occasions I have told you that in this court we do admit hearsay evidence, and it is for the Court to decide on the probative value of hearsay evidence. You may go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I asked if I could say this, and this is certainly the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. And the Tribunal has allowed you to say this. I would like to just clarify something with regard to this statement. This is a statement that you heard from Fahrudin Ahmic. Which Fahrudin Ahmic are we talking about? Where did he live and what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was a very nice man, very nice. He had three children. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Perhaps it might be useful if the witness could be shown the map, 273?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you, using the pointer, just try to find the house of Fahrudin Ahmic just so we know where he lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: The house of Fahrudin Ahmic is over here (indicating). Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Again, Drago Josipovic's house, if you could show us where that is again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's right over here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: So this Fahrudin Ahmic lived right next door to the Josipovic house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were nearby. The road towards Hasim's house, that is Fahrudin's father, and Fahrudin's house was the only thing that divided Hasim's house and the house of the parents of Drago Josipovic, and behind Drago Josipovic -- rather, it is Drago Josipovic's parents and then Drago. That's the way the houses went. Because there was one road that led to Fahrudin's house and then there was Drago Josipovic's parents' house, right over there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, I want to just take you back just for a second. If we could go back to the diagram, usher, please? As you were, and your children, as you were walking to position "C," did you notice anything with regard to the soldiers either on the veranda or elsewhere, and now I'm talking about a time period in between your leaving the veranda and arriving at position "C," as you were walking towards position "C"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: These soldiers who were standing on the steps, they all walked into the house at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, after you arrived at position "C," did you speak with your mother, and if so, do you recall what she told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we came to her, she told me over there, "Two men in helmets took Muzafer away." That was all; we didn't speak any more. Because bullets were flying all over, we leaned against this wall, as I was holding my children; she was here; and I said, "Mama, let's go into the shed." "Okay." Although that was no guarantee for our lives. But, you know, a person thinks that he can save himself that way at such moments, so we walked into this shed. I placed my children here in front of me (indicating) and we were huddling, and there were some wooden boards here, and I was there behind my children and behind me was my mother. Then I put my hands on their heads, like this, and I was clutching them all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you, with the marker, place the letter "D" to show us now the fourth position that you and your children, and now mother, were in that morning so that we can refer to it in future?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If you could place the letter "D" so it's not so small that we can't read it? Just to symbolise where you were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, while you were at this position "D," which is in the room marked 7 on the schematic, could you see out of that room or was there a door blocking your view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I could see. This shed didn't have a door. The door was next to the window, but then it didn't have a window either. We had bought a window and a door, but they remained in the garage. So I could see, let's say, this area (indicating). Over here, I could only see this area, the corner of this house, that. But here, I had a better view, on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you had said that you noticed some of the soldiers going into your house, the soldiers who were on the veranda. Did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: -- see any other soldiers in the vicinity of your house at this time, either in the garden or in the yard or on the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Over here, in this area, yes. Over here (indicating). That's where the window is. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: So that would be near the corner of your house on the upper right-hand side as we look at this diagram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you recognise any --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you recognise any of those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, what is the next thing you remember seeing or hearing as you and your children and mother were in position "D"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we were sitting there and while I was holding my children's heads -- I don't know. I can't really tell the time because there was no way I could tell the time. Some minutes went on forever and others -- I don't know. So I saw soldiers jumping out of here and they were moving in this direction, towards Zarko's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, when you say you saw soldiers jumping out of "here," what do you mean by "here"? Could you describe where you saw soldiers as they jumped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Tell us where you saw the soldiers when they were jumping. Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard the thump when they jumped, like this, and they were passing by here, in front. Here (indicating). In front of the door and the window where we were crouching, you know, like I'm crouching here, and they're passing here, right in front.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Just to make it clear for the record, and correct me if I'm wrong, but you heard soldiers jumping, basically, off your veranda; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you heard them jumping. Did you see them as they left your house, or did you just hear them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard them and I saw them. I heard them and I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because they were walking here, this way (indicating). I could see them. I didn't lift my head, but -- I was afraid, but I saw these soldiers jumping out and passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, at that moment, did you recognise any of those soldiers as they passed by or jumped out of your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I wasn't watching their faces then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What is the next thing you recall? and now I'm specifically drawing your attention to your house after these soldiers passed by and left your house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: It all became quiet. No one was walking. You couldn't hear anyone. Silence. I felt smoke coming from my house, and I told my mama, I said, "Mama, the house is on fire." I felt this smoke getting out. I saw smoke from the terrace passing here. Lots of smoke. Since I couldn't hear anyone and I didn't see anyone, I tried to save my house. My mother did too. I said already that in this area, I had a storage space covered in ceramic tiles. It also had running water, a faucet. At that tap, I kept a hose, 20 or 30 metres long, and that is how I tended my cows, because I had two cows. Also the garden, the yard, et cetera. So this hose was over there at the tap. At that moment, I left my children, and mama, and I ran into the house. I rushed into the storage space, I grabbed this hose, I opened the water, and I went into this hallway, I went into the living room, and I tried to extinguish the fire with this hose. The house had a staircase too and there was a lot of wood, and also there was -- there were carpets, woollen carpets, and I kept trying to extinguish the fire with this water, we managed to do so, and then I went back there and joined my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: After, you joined your children and your mother back at position "D"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, I'm sorry. My mother was with me, together with me. Together we were trying to extinguish the fire and the children were alone. We left the children on their own while we were trying to extinguish the fire in the house, and then the two of us came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You were successful in extinguishing the fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: After a short time they came with inflammable bullets from the direction of Zarko's house, and unfortunately, my house was once again set fire to. It started burning, and I said to my mother, "We shouldn't go out again. We can't do anything this time. They can wound us with a bullet, they can hit us. My children are here." And so my mother said, "All right. We'll stay."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, if you can just remove the diagram that's in front of you and go to the map and show us where Zarko's house is so we know what you mean when you say the bullets came from Zarko's direction. You can use the pointer to show us Zarko's house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Zarko's house is this (indicating). From this direction -- the bullets came from that direction, hitting my house again and setting it on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What is the next thing you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were in the shed. We waited for our fate. My house was ablaze. Some parts had already begun to cave in. I looked at the house that belongs to Ramiz Ahmic and his sons, and Ramiz Ahmic had annexes. He was a rich man, so he had auxiliary buildings around his house. I said to my mother, "There's -- I'm happy to see that Ramiz's house is not on fire. He might give us a room to save ourselves and to shelter there until we find somewhere to go, because our house is completely destroyed. But never mind, we'll put this in order, this part here that's left, and we'll be able to live there." But houses were not on fire, they were intact, whereas my house was completely ablaze. I look at their houses and I was very happy to see that they were not alight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you, on that map in front of you, point to Ramiz's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. You just told me to point, to indicate Ramiz's house. This is Ramiz Ahmic's house (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: From where you were at position "D", could you see Ramiz's house well or was it obstructed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I could see it well. It's an open space. There's nothing to obstruct my view, so I could see his house directly from where I stood, and his whole entire property, and Nazif's as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What did you see then, or hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: After some time had elapsed, I heard, along this path here, from the direction of Zarko's house, there was thumping, the thump of footsteps could be heard, and I heard Ivanka talking, but I don't know who she was talking to. Then perhaps one, two, three minutes later I saw, from this direction where I was standing, I saw a group of soldiers passing by the road, the path up there, and they left. I don't know where they went.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you replace that diagram on the machine next to you so we can see where you were pointing, because we couldn't see it as you were pointing now. Perhaps the usher can assist.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: What do you want me to show you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you show us where you heard the soldiers pass by? What road were they on and in what direction were they going?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were here, from the direction of Zarko's house, and they went in this direction (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You've indicated that with an arrow along the right-hand side of the diagram; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were going up to the main road leading to the other road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: On that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: On that occasion, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned hearing the voice of Ivanka. Who is Ivanka?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you see her or did you just hear her voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I just heard her. I didn't see her, couldn't see her, just heard her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: After the soldiers passed, did you hear anything coming from the houses of Nazif or Ramiz?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: When they passed this way and after several minutes, I saw here, in this direction, a group of soldiers in this part here (indicating). They had passed by, but I couldn't see where they had gone to from where I was standing. Then as I kept looking at their houses, I saw that in this way, as I'm showing you now, a group of soldiers went towards Ramiz's house, that is to say they came to the shed first, and below the shed is the manure, it was all concrete cement, and they went towards that part. One portion went down into the place where the manure is stored, the others went by the shed or whatever it was, and then I heard voices, "Come out you balijas so that we can cut your throats. Come out you balijas, we're going to slaughter you." The soldiers went further upwards, and I could no longer see them because they were moving up towards the front of the house, because the house and the shed is there. They entered the yard and I couldn't see them anymore, but I heard them. Before that, I heard Nazif's wife's voice, and there was a sort of struggle, a fight, and then the voice disappeared. I heard Ramiz shouting, "What's up people? What's up? What do you want? What is all this? What's happening?" I didn't hear the soldiers anymore, but I did hear Ramiz, in a very sad voice saying, "Wife, come out. Let them see you. Let them see you. Come out." Those were the last voices that I heard. I didn't hear Ramiz anymore, and I didn't hear anything anymore of that incident. Later on, I saw, on the lower floor of the house, one of Ramiz's rooms on fire. I could see flames and smoke, and, of course, the flames spread.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Were you in a position to be able to identify or recognise any of those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, how long did you stay at position "D"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: The whole day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: When did you leave position "D", do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: How did that come about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I left towards evening. It wasn't very dark yet but it was dusk. As in the course of the day, Jozo Livancic had come up to us. I don't know how he came. I didn't see -- I saw him. He sort of had some rubber soles or something, because he was quite silent. We didn't hear him come up, we just saw him. He came up to us and looked at us like this (indicating), up to the door that was free, and he saw me and my mother sitting on the plank and saw our children with us, and he just left. My mother called out to him. She said, "Jozo, Jozo," but he didn't respond. He didn't want to turn around at all or say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, tell us who Jozo Livancic is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: He is the father of Zeljo Livancic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: By the way, that position "D" in the toolshed marked number 7, during the day, did you or your mother do anything to attempt to provide yourselves with some additional protection, and I'm referring specifically to the doorway.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, I did, because when Jozo Livancic had left, not much time had gone by. From this corner here, a bullet hit directly here (indicating). I stood there and God saved me, nobody else. My hair was singed, and the bullet hit the wall where the cows were. I crouched down again in fear, waiting to see if there would be another one that would follow it. There was nothing. A silence, a lull. Then as we were in the toolshed and we had some tools from the car and car tires, I placed planks against the window and then lifted the part of the car, the hub of the car, and I kept it up as protection against the windows so that they should not hit my children. I was only frightened that something would happen to my children or my mother. By the door I placed another plank. I held all this material in this position, and I stayed there holding everything up until Josip -- Jozo Livancic and Drago Papic came to that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: This would have been just before dark on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, during the course of the day, while you were in position "D", did you ever look around your house to see where your husband might be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, I just had this view of the front part of the house. But I kept saying to myself -- I kept consoling myself, and I lived in the hope that my neighbours had taken my husband prisoner. That's what I said to myself. Nobody told me that, I just said this to myself to give me strength and to console myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, during the course of the day while you were in position "D", did you hear any shooting or any other sounds that you can describe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was the shooting the whole day. There was shelling the whole day. Shooting throughout the day, grenades, mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, I think you said just a moment ago that towards evening some people came to the shed. Could you tell us who those people were who came to the shed, that is position "D"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: They didn't come into the shed, they came in front of the shed, to the shed, and they were Drago Josipovic, in full military gear; Papic Drago, once again full military gear; and Jozo Livancic, also in full military gear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned "Papic." Which Papic was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were two. No. One is Drago. Papic Anto is an elderly man. He's well-built, tall, and he used to live below the house of Ramic Kijazim, along that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Was the elderly man, the elderly Papic, was he the one that was at the toolshed that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: All three of them were standing like this in the same position. All three of them stood in front of my shed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you have any difficulty recognising Drago Josipovic as one of those three men who was standing in front of your shed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I recognised all three of them. They're all neighbours. They were not unknown men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What happened when they came to the shed, just outside the shed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: They called out to me (redacted) come out, come out. Come out." I said, "I don't dare come out. My children are here," I said. So he said, "Come out, all of you," and we had to go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What happened when you, your children and your mother came out, exited the shed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic told me, "Your shed is going to be set afire now." I said, "All right. Just leave my cows. Let them out so that they're not burnt alive."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What did Drago Josipovic then do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: We had a big hammer, and he cut off the lock of the door to the cow shed. He bashed the door down and he let the cows go out of the shed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: So that was, in fact, an act of some kindness towards the animals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Then where did you and your mother and children go? Before you answer, please hold on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Moskowitz, could we clarify which of the Papic's it was?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Certainly. I would be happy to do it or the Court can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Let's be absolutely clear, witness. Could you describe the Papic who was at your toolshed that evening with the other two men, Drago Josipovic and Jozo Livancic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: About how old was this man, this Papic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: An elderly man. Perhaps about 60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The reference is to Anto, clearly, not Dragan.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I suppose that he is about 60 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps he's a year or two older, but thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you know this man's first name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Anto Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us what your family did after the cows were released by Drago Josipovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: They then said to us the following: "Go into the house down there," that is to say, Anto Papic's house, "there are some more Muslims down there."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, go to Anto Papic's house that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I told them that I didn't dare go, because I had seen terrible things happen, and I told them, "I don't dare go. You come with us."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: They said, "All right." We were wearing pyjamas, we were barefoot, and they went along with us towards the house of Anto Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you put any kind of clothing on that you found in the toolshed before you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes. I put on some of my late husband's old trousers, his work trousers. He used them for work when he was in the toolshed. I had an old jumper which I used when I went to milk the cows. That's what I put on, and that's what I wore when I left. The children didn't put anything else on, they left as they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, could you, perhaps with the assistance of the usher, again, look at the map and show us the direction that you took to go to Anto Papic's house that evening? You can use the pointer, I think, to show the route.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we left my shed here, we took this route (indicating). We crossed over here. There was a small concrete wall. We went along this path up to Zarko's house, and then past Zarko's house further on to this road here, and we went along the road this way, and arrived at the house of Anto Papic. It was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: For future reference, could you help us again by taking the marker and drawing a line showing your route from the house, your house -- or your shed, to the house of Anto Papic? You could take the diagram off the maps while you're doing that so it's easier for you to draw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Do you mean across this -- on this map here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Which colour shall I use, red?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I think red would show up best. Perhaps the usher could help with the handling of the diagram.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Very well. (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I would ask the usher to show the witness the next exhibit for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 276.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: This is a photograph that we call Exhibit 276. Witness, could you identify that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is the house of Mr. Papic Anto.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That would be the house that has the letter "F" over it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: There's a path that we see in front of the picture. Is that the path that you and your family took that evening when you went to Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: When you entered this house, who did you see there, if anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really did see a lot of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Were these women, and children and men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were women, there were children and there were men as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you see anyone you knew and can tell us about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of the Muslims, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Who did you see there that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I recognised them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you speak with any of them and did they tell you anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I went into the house (redacted) they were all very sad. They were all crying(redacted) cried aloud, and she said, (redacted) (redacted) and you know that your husband has been killed as well." That's what she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you at that time know that your husband had been killed, in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic told(redacted) that, and Drago Josipovic told me, when I was in front of the shed, in this kind of tone, "Ah (redacted)has been killed too”.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you stay overnight at Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Was anyone taking care of the children at Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was the wife of Anto Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you see how she was taking care of the children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you know what? There were a lot of cows belonging to the Muslims. They all came to the yard. There were a lot of cows, and my cows were there too. I asked whether I could go out to milk my cows to give my children some milk and to drink some milk myself and then what's left could be shared by the others, and they said, "Yes, you can." That's what I did. They milked the cows too. They cooked the milk and they gave the children milk to drink and anybody else who wanted to drink, although all of us who knew what was going on and who had seen what was going on, we didn't really feel like eating, and the lady brought some other food which she offered to the children, she gave them some other food as well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I note the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have many more questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I have several questions plus a short video, so it may be appropriate to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. So we will adjourn now for 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Moskowitz, we will go on, continuing in open session, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, Madam, we will continue where we left off, and that is at the house of Anto Papic. While you were at the house of Anto Papic, did there come a time that several of the Muslim men were asked to do something, and if so, could you tell us what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: While you and your family were at the house of Anto Papic, you stated that there were several Muslim families also at the house of Anto Papic. Did there come a time that some of these Muslim men were asked to leave the house to do something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: The same day, on the 16th of April, you mean? In the evening, towards dusk, when we had arrived; is that what you're asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At any time during your stay at the Papic house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: That the men, the Muslims, asked to do something, that they should do something or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: While you were at the Anto Papic house, did you see any of your Croatian neighbours there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Who did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I saw Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic in front of us, as soon as we arrived. Livancic Jozo was there too, but I didn't see him after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: The next day, did you see any additional Croatian neighbours at or near the Anto Papic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: The following day --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- when dawn broke, yes. There was a window in the room, and I saw in the yard Nenad Santic. There were other soldiers there as well of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us who Nenad Santic was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was a company commander, captain in the HVO.(redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Again, with the assistance of the usher, could the usher have the witness look at the map of Ahmici, which is 273.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Would you point to the house of Nenad Santic, if you can find it there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: May I pick up the photograph to have a better look?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nenad Santic's house, you enter it this way (indicating). There it is. That's where it stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Nenad Santic, is he related to any of the individuals that you have already mentioned in your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Who is he related to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: He is related to Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What is that relationship?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic's wife Slavica is Nenad Santic's sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not Slavica belonged to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: She dealt with that sort of thing a great deal, and on one occasion, when we went to work, as the buses were not working, we waited at the bus stop to get somebody to take us to work, and without thinking anything bad, I had the best intentions, I wanted to get in her car, but she pushed me away from the doorway, and she says, "You balija can't come in here." She took in an elderly woman, a cleaning woman, in Vitez, she worked in a work organisation, and she invited her into the car, and she said, "She can come in, but not you." So I stayed at the bus stop alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you said you saw Nenad Santic in the Anto Papic yard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What do you recall of what he did or said that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not hear what he said. He was outside with his soldiers, but from amongst them, Anto Papic went into the house straightaway, and he said the following: That the men should get up and go and pick up our dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did the men, the Muslim men, do that? Did they leave the house, the Anto Papic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did those Muslim men return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Several hours later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Would you tell us when and how you and your family left the Anto Papic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: When the people who went to pick up the dead returned -- I can't tell you exactly what time it was, whether it was 11.00 or what the time was but somewhere in that region -- when they returned, Anto Papic said that Nenad, that Nenad had said -- this is what Anto Papic said: "Nenad has ordered you to go to Zume. A bus will be waiting for you there to take you to Zenica."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Then did you and the others leave the Anto Papic house as you were ordered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: We went up towards the main asphalt road leading to Travnik, towards Vitez. That is to say, towards the main road going to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: When you reached the main road, did you see anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the very exit where this road ends, I saw a tank go by. We asked assistance from the tank. This is what -- we made signs to the tank to stop, and the tank stopped. As we don't know -- can't speak English or German, he asked us something, we didn't understand him, but we asked assistance, we asked them to evacuate us from that spot, but we weren't able to make ourselves understood. Then one soldier from within the tank got out of the tank and told us -- and I'll get up, if I may? I apologise for doing so, but I would like to show you. He said, "Has the HVO taken you all?" And we said "Yes." We thought that these people would help us. Unfortunately, they didn't help us. The tank moved on and we followed it as fast as we could. When it was between Drago Josipovic's house and another house, there's an open space there, Drago Josipovic was standing there and Anto Papic was standing there as well, and this soldier from the tank beckoned to them, to the two of them, to come up to him. This is the sign he made (indicating). Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic went up to the soldier -- there's a little fence there. This is the road. We were standing on the road by the tank. There's a small hedge there. The two of them went up to this hedge. Anto Papic could speak German because he received some money from Germany by way of rent, it was a sort of pension, a pension that he received from Germany -- I used to make up the papers for him -- so he spoke German. They said something, but we couldn't understand what they were saying. We saw, at the end of their conversation, that the tank had left us; that is, they withdrew -- the two of them withdrew to where they were before. The tank left, and we were left standing in the road alone stranded. We moved in the direction of Zume, as Nenad had ordered, thinking that a bus would be waiting for us there. Unfortunately, what waited for us was the camp. We walked along the road, and then we turned to the right past Vidosevic Anto's house, there is a path going that way, and in that road, there is a row of houses along that path, and they took us in in one of those houses. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Just to clarify your testimony a little bit. Could you look at that Exhibit 273, which is the blow-up and, using the pointer, show us the route you took that day from Anto Papic's house to the house where you ended up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we came out this way, we met the tank, and I told you what we asked. The tank moved forward, and we followed it this way. The tank stopped here. We were all standing around. He called to the two of them, and they were standing here in this part. They came up to the soldier, talked to him in German. When they had finished their conversation -- I don't know what conclusion they had come to -- but the tank left us standing there without giving us any explanation whatsoever. We stayed standing there alone, and then we walked up the road this way and we came to this point here (indicating). Just let me study the map, if I may, for one second? Yes, that's all right. As I say, we came to this corner here where we turned right, and we were taken into one of these houses. I don't know which one. This is a new house, it belongs to Ivo Vidovic, and the two here, I don't really remember which house we were placed in because I was busy thinking about other things. I had other things on my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, again with the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: But they placed us in one of those houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you. With the help of the usher, perhaps you could take the green marker and draw a line from Anto Papic's house to the house you arrived at, showing the route you took to get from Anto Papic's house to that house in Santici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Anto Papic's house to their so-called -- I don't know. They had some kind of headquarters, the HVO, over there. It used to be a store. But at that time it wasn't a store. That is where they were staying. So from Anto Papic's house all the way up to this place where they were staying, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes, if you could, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks). I don't know where we were taken in exactly, whether in one or the other house, but it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you put an "X" where you saw Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic speaking to the tank driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. (Marks) That's where they were. They came up to this point here, and they were standing there when he beckoned to them and when he asked them to come up to him. This is a hedge and this is the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Were Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic in a uniform at the time or in uniforms at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and with weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, as you walked down to that HVO headquarters, as you called it, that shop in Santici, could you see the condition of the village of Ahmici from the road as you walked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you describe what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: I saw that the Muslim houses had all been burnt. Only the roof to Fahrudin Ahmic's house was intact at that time. Everything else had been burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, when you entered the house in Santici, the HVO headquarters, what did you see there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: We saw the room, there was some vinyl tiles on the floor, and the Muslims went into the room. They were full of fear. There were boys there, little -- bigger boys. (redacted) (redacted) and that my other neighbours, the men, had been killed, and the wives were in that room. All of us were sad. Everybody was crying. Some people were sitting round the wall. We all sat down on the floor. We were too tired and weary and didn't feel like anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did something happen while you were there, something that you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Tell us about that. What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Two HVO soldiers entered the room. They had the black socks over their heads with just slits for the eyes. All you could see were their eyes. One of them was fairly tall, the other one was a little shorter in build, and as we knew him personally, we concluded that it was Nikica Plavcic. We called him "Nikica Slikica," slikica being a picture, and he was a photographer, in fact. The tall one entered the room where we were located. I'm going to show you -- I apologise, but I'm going to demonstrate how this went -- he entered the room and he looked around, like this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (redacted) he said, “You, you, you, you, you, let’s go.”(redacted) and she said "Please don't take him away. He has a bad kidney and he has to have dialysis. Please don't take him away." "Don't worry about that," they said, "He'll be cured very quickly." Ramic Zenur, his brother Amir, and Mr. Engineer Heleg Munib went out. A little boy from Loncari, he was fairly tall and thin, he managed, as the door was here and the women had lined up against this door, when he left, he hid behind the women and crouched down. That's how he stayed. He stayed alive by crouching and hiding behind the line of women. Fahrudin's father, Hasim, Munib Heleg got up and the two brothers, they left following them. They went in the direction of Slamo, the late Slamo, Mujo Dedic, Fariz, Siljak -- I'll remember his name in a little while -- but that's where they were taken. Nobody knows what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did Hasim and the other Muslim men who were taken, did they return at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did (redacted), ever find out what happened to her husband, (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Since we were imprisoned there, there were babies, and we tried to ask UNPROFOR for help because UNPROFOR was going up and down this road. Women with small babies would go out when this UNPROFOR would come 13 by, but it was all in vain. (redacted) stood there at the door. I was next to her. There were more of us there. We were waiting for some kind of help. After some time, Nikica Plavcic came, and the women asked him, "Please, don't you see that we have babies? The babies are hungry. Can you do something? Can you have us evacuated?" He looked at us and he said, "Well, let her go there to the road." He was pointing at me. He said, "She can stop a vehicle and you can go." I said, "I didn't bring anyone here, and it is not up to me to stop UNPROFOR." (redacted) asked him, "Nikica, please. Where is my (redacted)? Please tell me. Where did they go?" He said, "Don't worry. They were taken to Busovaca." Again, a bit of time went by, and again (redacted) said "Nikica, please, tell me where is my

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: (redacted)was impatient. She was on very good terms with his late mother, Nikica's late mother. "Nikica, please." His mother had died of cancer. "Nikica, please, I beseech you, in the name of your dead mother. You know that we were very good friends. Tell me, where is my (redacted)." He looked at her and said, "Orders were issued and they were all killed." Then we withdrew and sat on those plastic tiles down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Where were you taken -- let me ask you this: How long did you spend at that house in Santici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, we were brought there on the 17th. I think it was around noon. That was a Saturday. We spent the night there, the night between Saturday and Sunday, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: How did it come about that you left that house and where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the morning, they were discussing something amongst themselves, I don't know what they were talking about, but at any rate, they told us again, "Go to the station and you'll go to Zenica."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Before we leave that house, let me ask you just a couple more questions. Do you know a man by the name of Abdulah Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you see him at that house in Santici while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he came there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What did he look like when you saw him there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Terrible. Terrible. He looked terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? What did you see with regard to any injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he came and he was sitting right in front of me. He was all dirty. His head was stained by blood a bit and his head was swollen. He was a sight, really. He looked terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you see any children who were not accompanied by parents or adults?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you know the Zec family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you see any member of the Zec family at that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the little Melisa. Melisa is her name. A pretty little girl, pretty. She was there, not her brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You say her brother was not there with her?
