utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he was not there with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, where did you and the others go when you left the house on Sunday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Where we went, is that what you're saying? Would you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes. Where did you go when you left the house on Sunday, you and the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: We went to the railway station, we call it the Kompanija, and they put us up at the school in Dubravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: By "they" do you mean the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly, yes. They were the ones who commanded us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: How did you get from the house to the Dubravica school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: On foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: How long did you spend at the Dubravica school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Until the 1st of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you remember how you were released from the Dubravica school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Tell us how that happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: A girl came from Geneva, a pretty girl, she had a braid. Also an interpreter called Alma. They came one day, and we thought that all of us would get out, that we would leave the camp. Unfortunately, we received the news that we couldn't, that we would be staying there. What the reason was for that I do not know. I do know that on the next day, Alma, this interpreter, showed up again, a blonde girl, pretty, with freckles on her face. She said, "Today you will be getting out of here," and we were happy, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not any of this was videotaped or put on a camera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. When we were supposed to get out, we were supposed to give them some kind of signatures. I was staying in this room with my mother and my children, and I was the first one there. The door was there and then I was right next to the door, and next to me was a refugee from Prijedor, and also an old Granny with her daughter and her granddaughter. Her sons had also been killed. When they came in and asked for us to come and give these signatures, we were the first to go, my children, my mother and I, and we were afraid. I didn't know where we were going. They said, "Come along," and we followed them. We walked into a room. There was a table there, and Ivanka Miskovic was sitting there. She had a typewriter, and she was a typist. She worked in Veternica. We knew each other very well, but that morning she didn't know me. She asked me what my name was, what my children's names were, what my mother's name was, things like that. We did that. By her was Nikica Plavcic, like this. Brown hair, pretty tall. He wasn't fat. Sort of elegant. In a HVO uniform. When I signed this paper he said to me, "Madam, you can go to your home now, there's no problem whatsoever." I said to him, "Sir, you killed all of my own. You burned down everything of my own and now you're sending me home." "Just a minute, let me see what we're going to do with such cases." He went out. When he came back, I think that there were some American journalists there with him. I don't know if there were three -- there were three of them there. I don't know. I saw cameras. I saw them, a blonde lady, kind and nice. They walked in and they started filming us straightaway. My daughter started to cry. She asked me how I felt at the camp, and I answered to her, "Madam, you know what it's like in a camp. A camp is a camp. I'm allergic to dust and look at me, I'm all in blisters. Look." I said, "I don't want to talk about the food and all the details." Mr. Plavcic said, "What do you mean? We treated you nicely." I said, "No. No way. You didn't treat us to anything. What you treated us to were the food that Muslims from Novaci, above the school, brought to us," and they allowed them to bring it in because there were babies, there were a lot of people there, there were men, women, elderly people, people who were weak, and these people really did their best to send things to us. We would get something, my mother and I, but we gave it to my children so that they could survive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At this time I would ask if we could view the video, which would be the next Prosecution Exhibit. We do have a translation prepared for the voices that you hear on the video, although it's very disconnected and difficult to follow in terms of the voices, but the visual, I think, is what's important.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: May I ask something? Is there anyone who gets killed on this film? Will I see anything like that, like people getting killed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video will be marked 277, and the transcript 277A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would like to ask the Prosecutor to tell us when this tape was filmed, and who filmed it and when. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. That's an apposite question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, this tape was filmed at, or on or about the time of the release from the Dubravica school, so it would be late April, early May of 1993. It appears to be a film either made by the Red Cross itself or by a news organisation. But it shows the inside of the Dubravica school, and it shows several of the detainees that this witness recognises, and it, in fact, shows this witness at the school with her children.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, witness, as you look at the film, and we have looked at this before, have we not, you and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecutor did not say how this tape came into his possession and how he obtained it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Moskowitz, can you tell us how you got this tape?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At this point I don't know exactly how we got this tape, but I can endeavour to get those answers and report back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What I am confident in is that like a photograph, this videotape can be identified by this witness who was there to observe the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Again, witness, in answer to your question earlier about seeing unpleasant scenes of death, no, this will not have any of that. This is a videotape that you and I have already looked at.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE (Resumed)
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Moskowitz, can we see this in open session, this videotape?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: We will see the face of several people that we probably don't want to have shown in open session, unless the video is going to somehow not be broadcast outside this room.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: At the moment, it will, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I think it ought to be in closed session then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. Moskowitz?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Mr. President, just to report back on the origin of the tape. I am informed that the tape was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on June 17, '97, and it was a tape compiled by Dan Damon (phoen), who is a reporter, I think, for one of the news channels that covered the conflict in Bosnia, and that there are several different segments on this tape, and the segment that we saw was taken in May of '93, although the exact date of that segment is not clear on the information I have. So that is the information on the tape. Now, also there is one other matter that has come to my attention. The witness, Mr. Whitworth, who is to follow the witness that is presently scheduled for cross-examination, this witness is, in fact, a teacher in England and has very pressing obligations with his class. It was quite difficult to fit him into the schedule of our presentation. He does request that his testimony be completed today so that he can return to his class tomorrow. Apparently he is running a camp for children and they need him badly for that. We have spoken briefly with Defence counsel about the possibility, with the Court's approval, of allowing Mr. Whitworth to testify now and then continue with the cross-examination of the other witness afterward, but I am informed that the Defence counsel would not agree to that, will not agree to that, and nevertheless we make the request of the Court to see if that can be done, and if that cannot be done, to consider an alternative, that the Tribunal will sit long enough today so that it will be assured that Mr. Whitworth can finish his testimony today so he can return to England.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence has been informed of the request made by the Prosecution. We do have every understanding for the responsibilities of the witness in question, but we feel that the Defence has the right to cross-examination immediately after having the Prosecution examine her, and we would like to proceed to cross-examination immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. All right. We may go on until 5.45, and we will also take shorter breaks in the hope that we can settle this matter. All right. So we will go on with the cross-examination of Witness EE. While you are there, Mr. Moskowitz, would it be correct to say that in paragraph 32 of the indictment, there is a slight factual mistake where it is mentioned that this lady was there "while the family, which included two young daughters."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That would be a factual error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: A factual error.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: It is a daughter and a son.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: A daughter and son. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you for drawing our attention to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. So we will now call the -- somebody is going to bring in the witness. Counsel Pavkovic, who is going to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to inform you that I shall be cross-examining the witness first myself, then we will hear Defence counsel Susak and Mr. Ranko Radovic, as well as Mrs. Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac. Mrs. Slokovic has just told me that she won't be examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So you yourself, Counsel Susak, and Counsel Radovic then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. (The witness entered court).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Pavkovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, in view of the fact that in my cross-examination, I shall be mentioning a number of names and I shall be speaking of circumstances which indirectly could hinder the rights of this witness to protection, I would like to have the session behind closed doors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will go into a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
